Start with "0. Log in". Requests go through the gateway ({{baseUrl}}) unless marked.

The slug is derived from the name. A client-chosen slug is a client choosing a URL, and two would collide in a way only the unique index notices.
Child categories move up to this one's parent and products keep existing -- only the membership links go. A taxonomy edit must never be able to delete something sellable.

item.name: Rename, move or reposition a category

request.description: Partial: null fields are left alone. Renaming does NOT change the slug -- it is in storefront URLs and in anyone's bookmarks, so the label and the address are separate concerns.

item.name: One product by id, including DRAFT and ARCHIVED
Upload an image for a product

request.description: JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 5 MB. The bytes are re-encoded: EXIF is applied and then stripped (so a supplier's GPS coordinates are not published and the photograph is not left sideways), and the stored content type comes from decoding the file rather than from the request. Uploading the same bytes twice returns the first image.

item.name: Image bytes for any product, published or not
Delete one of a product's images
Publish a product, if it has an active variant priced above zero
Add a variant to a product
The category tree, roots first, each with its children nested
Image bytes for a published product

request.description: Served with a one-year immutable cache and a strong ETag taken from the stored content hash. Returns 404 -- not 403 -- when the owning product is not ACTIVE, because a 403 would confirm that the image exists. Range requests are ignored and the full entity is returned.

item.name: Product types with their declared attributes, in display order
List published products, filtered and sorted

request.description: Returns ACTIVE products only. DRAFT and ARCHIVED are never listed, which is also why the catalogue looks empty immediately after the variants migration: it left every pre-existing product DRAFT because none of them had a price anyone had chosen. `orderBy` is named that way rather than `sort` so it does not collide with Spring's own paging `sort` parameter, and it is a closed set of values because the ordering has to be built into SQL -- a caller-supplied sort expression would be an injection. `category` matches the category AND its descendants, so filtering by a parent returns everything beneath it. An unknown category slug is a 400, unlike an unknown `tag`, which answers 200 with an empty page: a tag is a free-form label whose absence means nothing, while a category is a closed set. Price filtering uses the cheapest PURCHASABLE variant -- active and priced above zero -- so a deactivated or unpriced variant cannot pull a product into a price band a customer cannot actually buy at.

item.name: Who owns the catalog service, and how to reach them
One product by id, enriched with stock availability
Resolve prices for up to 100 variants

request.description: Read-only despite being a POST: the identifier list is too long for a URL. Each requested id is answered with a status of PRICED, UNPUBLISHED or UNKNOWN, in request order. An UNPUBLISHED entry deliberately carries no price, so a caller that skips the status check fails loudly rather than charging for something that is not for sale.
